headline: Representative James Clyburn Backs Expanding Supreme Court to 13 Justices
summary: Representative James Clyburn endorsed expanding the Supreme Court from nine to 13 justices during a Sunday television interview. The South Carolina Democrat aligned his position with former Vice President Kamala Harris, citing the nation's 13 federal appellate circuits as historical precedent.
seoTitle: Clyburn Backs Expanding Supreme Court to 13 | Choseno
metaDescription: Representative James Clyburn endorses expanding the Supreme Court to 13 justices, aligning with federal appellate circuits.
tweet: Rep. James Clyburn endorses expanding the Supreme Court to 13 justices, aligning his stance with former VP Kamala Harris.
body:
WASHINGTON — Representative James E. Clyburn (D-S.C.) publicly endorsed expanding the Supreme Court of the United States to 13 justices on Sunday, August 30, 2026, aligning himself with growing calls among prominent Democrats to enact statutory structural reforms for the nation's highest judicial bench.

Speaking on NBC's "Meet the Press" with moderator Kristen Welker, Clyburn responded affirmatively when asked whether he supported former Vice President Kamala Harris's recent proposal to increase the size of the court from nine to 13 members. Clyburn characterized 13 as a historically and structurally logical number that directly corresponds to the modern organization of the federal appellate system.

"Yes, I do," Clyburn said during the broadcast. "Thirteen is a pretty good number. It's a baker's dozen, but it also reflects the 13 circuit courts of appeals that we have."

## Structural Rationale and Historical Precedent

The proposal to expand the bench to 13 seats reflects a deliberate alignment with the 13 federal judicial circuits, which comprise 11 numbered regional circuits, the District of Columbia Circuit, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. Proponents of the reform note that when Congress established the current nine-justice configuration under the Judiciary Act of 1869, the number of seats was explicitly set to match the nine judicial circuits that existed in the United States at that time.

Over the course of American history, the size of the Supreme Court has shifted repeatedly through congressional legislation. The Judiciary Act of 1789 originally established a six-member bench, which was subsequently adjusted to seven justices in 1807, nine in 1837, and ten in 1863 before being reduced to seven in 1866 and finally restored to nine in 1869. Because the United States Constitution grants Congress broad authority to establish and regulate the structure of the federal judiciary under Article III, statutory revisions to the court's composition do not require a constitutional amendment.

Clyburn's comments follow recent public remarks from former Vice President Kamala Harris, who delivered a speech at the National Urban League's annual convention in Nashville endorsing the 13-seat expansion. The synchronized positioning of senior Democratic leaders reflects an escalating focus on judicial reform within national civic discourse.

## Legislative Realities and Bipartisan Debate

Despite rising interest among progressive and mainstream Democrats, structural court reform proposals face substantial legislative and political hurdles on Capitol Hill. Under current Senate rules, any legislation to alter the composition of the Supreme Court requires overcoming the 60-vote filibuster threshold, creating a formidable barrier in a closely divided Congress.

Congressional Republicans have voiced staunch opposition to court expansion proposals, characterizing the initiative as an attempt at partisan court packing that would undermine the perceived institutional legitimacy and independence of the judicial branch. Critics caution that expanding the bench could trigger an escalating cycle of retaliatory additions whenever partisan control of the presidency and Congress changes hands.

Institutional moderates and legal scholars have also raised alternative reform models, such as establishing staggered 18-year term limits for justices or implementing binding ethical codes with external enforcement mechanisms.

## Midterm Strategy and Policy Prioritization

During the interview, Clyburn also addressed the Democratic Party's broader strategic posture ahead of upcoming midterm elections. While acknowledging the oversight powers available to a potential House majority, the veteran South Carolina lawmaker emphasized that the party must prioritize economic issues that directly affect working families over contentious procedural fights.

Clyburn urged candidates to concentrate on expanding healthcare access, lowering prescription drug costs, investing in workforce development, and expanding affordable housing supplies. He emphasized that durable civic trust depends on delivering tangible economic outcomes while preserving democratic norms and institutional integrity across all branches of government.

headline: Representative Ro Khanna Says 2028 Decision Independent of Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
summary: Representative Ro Khanna stated that a prospective 2028 presidential campaign by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez will have no bearing on his own political decisions. The California Democrat emphasized his distinct policy platform focused on economic patriotism, heartland manufacturing, and technological development.
seoTitle: Ro Khanna Discusses 2028 Race and AOC | Choseno
metaDescription: Representative Ro Khanna says a potential 2028 presidential run by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez will not affect his own political plans.
tweet: Rep. Ro Khanna says an AOC 2028 presidential run would have 'no bearing' on his own decision as he promotes economic patriotism.
body:
WASHINGTON — Representative Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) stated on Sunday, August 30, 2026, that a potential 2028 presidential campaign by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) would have "no bearing" on his own decision regarding whether to seek the Democratic presidential nomination.

Appearing on CNN's "State of the Union" with anchor Dana Bash, Khanna addressed questions regarding future national leadership and the evolving ideological landscape within the Democratic Party. When asked directly whether he would still launch a presidential bid if Ocasio-Cortez entered the primary contest, Khanna affirmed that his strategic considerations remain independent of other prospective candidates.

"It will have no bearing," Khanna told Bash during the broadcast. While praising his fellow progressive lawmaker as an "extraordinary politician" who commands a substantial national platform, Khanna outlined what he described as a distinct governing vision centered on industrial renewal, regional economic equity, and domestic manufacturing investment.

## Economic Patriotism and Industrial Revitalization

Khanna, who represents California's 17th congressional district encompassing Silicon Valley, has increasingly positioned himself as a national voice on economic revitalization and technological democracy. His proposed policy framework, termed "economic patriotism," advocates for substantial federal investments in domestic supply chains, clean energy manufacturing, and advanced technological infrastructure across historically deindustrialized regions of the United States.

Over recent months, Khanna has traveled extensively through traditional primary battlegrounds and industrial centers, including Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New Hampshire, and Iowa. In town halls and policy addresses, he has emphasized the necessity of bridging the economic divide between coastal high-tech hubs and heartland manufacturing towns that experienced factory closures and capital flight over past decades.

Khanna's platform focuses on expanding apprenticeship programs, incentivizing domestic semiconductor and battery production, supporting collective bargaining, and ensuring that emerging artificial intelligence technologies generate broadly distributed economic opportunities rather than concentrated wealth.

## Navigating the Progressive Coalition

The dialogue surrounding potential 2028 candidacies highlights broader strategic discussions within the Democratic Party regarding post-2024 coalition rebuilding. Political analysts observe that while Khanna and Ocasio-Cortez frequently collaborate on progressive legislative initiatives in the House of Representatives—including corporate accountability measures and healthcare reform—they articulate distinct approaches to electoral mobilization and coalition building.

Ocasio-Cortez has built an influential national grassroots movement with strong support among younger voters, urban working-class constituencies, and labor unions, emphasizing climate justice, universal social programs, and structural campaign finance reform. By contrast, Khanna has sought to cultivate a complementary lane by engaging both Silicon Valley entrepreneurs and Midwestern factory workers, arguing that technological innovation must be harnessed to rebuild American industrial power.

Democratic strategists note that a crowded primary field could offer party voters distinct perspectives on how best to regain working-class support and address economic anxieties.

## Legislative Focus Ahead of Midterm Elections

Despite national speculation about 2028 primary dynamics, Khanna emphasized that lawmakers must remain concentrated on immediate civic and economic challenges heading into upcoming congressional elections. He underscored that legislative progress on inflation reduction, affordable childcare, and infrastructure implementation remains paramount for regaining voter confidence across competitive districts.

Both Khanna and Ocasio-Cortez continue to serve in prominent committee assignments in the House of Representatives, where they have introduced measures targeting congressional stock-trading bans, defense procurement oversight, and worker retraining initiatives.

headline: Sen. Ted Cruz Defends Trump Administration's Iran Policy as Conflict Reaches Six-Month Mark
summary: Appearing on NBC's 'Meet the Press,' Senator Ted Cruz defended President Donald Trump's messaging on the ongoing conflict with Iran, describing military objectives as having distinct operational phases. Cruz asserted that initial strikes significantly dismantled Tehran's offensive capabilities, while an ongoing maritime blockade maintains economic pressure.
seoTitle: Cruz Defends Trump Iran Strategy on NBC | Choseno
metaDescription: Sen. Ted Cruz defended the Trump administration's Iran strategy on NBC's Meet the Press, citing degraded military infrastructure and ongoing economic pressure.
tweet: Sen. Ted Cruz outlined multiple phases of U.S. strategy in Iran on 'Meet the Press' as the conflict reaches its six-month milestone.
body:
During a Sunday appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press," United States Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) defended the Trump administration's execution of military and strategic objectives against Iran, as the broader international confrontation marked its six-month milestone. When questioned by moderator Kristen Welker regarding a graphic posted by President Donald Trump declaring "Mission Accomplished," Cruz argued that evaluating the campaign requires recognizing that the United States has pursued multiple distinct operational tracks since hostilities escalated in early 2026.

Cruz detailed what he characterized as significant degradation of the Islamic Republic of Iran's military posture, asserting that initial kinetic phases successfully neutralized core conventional and asymmetric threats. According to Cruz, allied and American operations have dismantled major portions of Iran's ballistic missile stockpiles, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) manufacturing infrastructure, and naval vessels operating in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Furthermore, Cruz pointed to the targeting of key command personnel within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as evidence that core military objectives intended to protect regional shipping and deter aggression have met defined strategic benchmarks set by military planners.

While acknowledging that active aerial bombardments have diminished in intensity, Cruz emphasized that military containment has transitioned into continuous economic and maritime enforcement. A central component of current U.S. strategy, Cruz highlighted, remains a comprehensive naval blockade and interdiction regime designed to restrict Iranian energy exports and sever illicit revenue streams. Cruz estimated that the economic enforcement mechanisms cost Tehran roughly $500 million per day in foregone revenue, describing the pressure campaign as an essential instrument to prevent the reconstitution of hostile regional infrastructure and ballistic programs.

The discussion highlighted ongoing congressional debates over the duration, legal authorization, and diplomatic endgame of American military engagements in the Middle East. Lawmakers on Capitol Hill remain divided along partisan and strategic lines regarding the scope of executive authority and the necessity of a formal Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF). Democratic leaders and several foreign policy analysts have cautioned that declaring missions accomplished prematurely risks underestimating regional instability, proxy resurgence, and humanitarian fallout across neighboring waterways. Conversely, Republican defense advocates maintain that targeted operations followed by sustained economic leverage represent a measured deterrent against further regional escalation.

Beyond the immediate scope of Middle Eastern foreign policy, Cruz's national television appearance touched upon broader domestic political dynamics and institutional governance. When asked about potential future political aspirations, including speculation surrounding the 2028 presidential cycle, Cruz demurred on immediate announcements, stating there would be appropriate timing to evaluate future electoral decisions. He also addressed state-level politics in Texas, expressing confidence in the state's Republican leadership and upcoming legislative priorities heading into the next election cycle.

As the conflict enters its second half-year, Congress is expected to conduct comprehensive oversight hearings through the Senate Foreign Relations and Armed Services Committees. Lawmakers are seeking updated intelligence assessments on Iranian nuclear enrichment capabilities, maritime safety for international commercial transit, and the long-term budgetary impact of ongoing naval deployments in the region. Cruz reiterated his commitment to supporting national defense readiness while demanding strict accountability regarding the enforcement of trade sanctions, international maritime laws, and military rules of engagement.

headline: Mayor Eddie Melton Demands Answers Following Extended Gary Power Outages
summary: Gary Mayor Eddie Melton announced ongoing municipal inquiries into the prolonged power outages that left tens of thousands without electricity following an August derecho. Melton called for utility accountability from NIPSCO and outlined relief coordination efforts for affected homeowners.
seoTitle: Gary Mayor Melton Probes Extended Power Outage | Choseno
metaDescription: Gary Mayor Eddie Melton addresses utility accountability, infrastructure repairs, and disaster relief following severe derecho power outages across the city.
tweet: Gary Mayor Eddie Melton is pressing utility providers for answers after severe storms caused extended power outages across Northwest Indiana.
body:
In the aftermath of an intense derecho storm that tore across Northwest Indiana in mid-August, City of Gary Mayor Eddie Melton announced that municipal leadership is actively investigating the systemic factors that led to two weeks of extended power outages for thousands of local residents. Speaking in an interview with CBS News on Sunday, Mayor Melton emphasized that although Northern Indiana Public Service Company (NIPSCO) has restored power to the overwhelming majority of affected customers, the city cannot treat the end of blackouts as a complete return to normal without addressing deep-rooted grid vulnerabilities and utility accountability.

The storm, which struck on August 11 with straight-line wind gusts clocked up to 99 miles per hour, caused severe damage across Lake County and knocked out electrical service to roughly 375,000 customers across NIPSCO's service territory. Gary emerged as one of the hardest-hit urban centers, with approximately 40,000 residents and businesses losing electricity. The prolonged disruption triggered critical public health challenges during mid-summer heat, resulting in extensive food spoilage, disruptions to wastewater management facilities, and acute safety concerns for elderly residents and individuals dependent on electrically powered medical equipment.

Mayor Melton, who brought fifteen years of prior professional experience at NIPSCO before entering elected office, offered direct scrutiny of the utility provider's response timeline and preventative maintenance practices. Melton asserted that the prolonged duration of the restoration effort was unacceptable for a modern municipal infrastructure network. Among the issues raised by city officials are questions regarding tree trimming schedules, vegetation management along high-voltage transmission corridors, aging distribution poles, and the initial deployment protocols of mutual aid crews during the emergency's critical early hours.

To mitigate the financial and structural toll on local homeowners, the City of Gary has mobilized localized support networks alongside state and federal relief channels. A notable bottleneck in the final restoration phase involved damaged weatherheads—the exterior connection fixtures that join private residential wiring to the municipal electrical grid. Because utility companies cannot legally connect power lines to damaged private service masts, the city partnered with community organizations, including the Legacy Foundation, to deploy licensed electrical contractors and cover repair expenses for vulnerable households facing costly out-of-pocket repairs.

The extended crisis has sparked broader regulatory scrutiny across Indiana. State leaders, including Indiana Governor Mike Braun, have called for formal reviews by the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC) to evaluate whether utility infrastructure investments and disaster preparedness protocols met required reliability standards. Simultaneously, affected residents and local community advocates have mobilized public forums and legal filings demanding equitable infrastructure reinvestment in historically underserved neighborhoods across the Rust Belt corridor.

Moving forward, Mayor Melton indicated that Gary will present a formal set of infrastructure modernization and communication demands to NIPSCO executives and state regulators. The municipal administration plans to establish community resilience hubs equipped with backup generator capacity, expand municipal emergency communication networks, and push for accelerated underground utility line pilot projects in heavily forested neighborhoods. Melton emphasized that ensuring long-term civic resilience will require sustained capital investment and transparent oversight rather than temporary emergency remedies.

headline: Pasco County Moves to Discontinue Right-of-Way Flock Surveillance Cameras Amid Privacy Debate
summary: Pasco County officials and the Sheriff's Office have agreed to end an interlocal automated license plate reader program, leading to the removal of roughly 60 roadside cameras by late September 2026. The decision follows intense community pushback over mass surveillance and data privacy, despite Sheriff Chris Nocco's warnings about impacts on crime investigations.
seoTitle: Pasco County Halts Flock Camera Dragnet | Choseno
metaDescription: Pasco County will remove roughly 60 automated license plate cameras following public privacy concerns, sparking debate with Sheriff Chris Nocco.
tweet: Pasco County will dismantle its roadside license plate camera program by September 30 following citizen privacy concerns, drawing sharp pushback from Sheriff Chris Nocco.
body:
In a notable shift for digital surveillance policy in Florida, the Pasco County Sheriff’s Office has announced the termination of its interlocal agreement governing automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras placed along public rights-of-way. The decision, scheduled to take effect on September 30, 2026, marks the end of the county government's direct participation in the roadside surveillance network and makes Pasco County one of the largest jurisdictions in the region to dismantle an established network of public ALPR hardware.

The municipal camera program was initially authorized by the Pasco County Board of County Commissioners in December 2024. Under that agreement, approximately 60 cameras manufactured by Flock Safety were installed on municipal roadside poles and intersections across unincorporated areas of the county. The camera system was configured to capture high-speed photographs of passing vehicles, logging license plate characters, vehicle makes, models, colors, and identifiable physical alterations into a searchable law enforcement database.

In recent months, the Sheriff’s Office sought to renegotiate its operational framework by transitioning from Flock Safety to Axon Enterprise, an alternative vendor whose systems integrated directly with deputies' body-worn cameras and existing digital evidence repositories. Officials stated the vendor swap aimed to lower recurring maintenance costs while consolidating evidence management. However, when the proposed vendor agreement appeared before the Board of County Commissioners in August 2026, it triggered an unexpected and intense wave of community opposition during public comment sessions.

Scores of Pasco County residents, local business owners, and civil liberties advocates packed commission chambers on August 11 and August 25 to express profound privacy concerns. Opponents argued that blanket ALPR networks create an unwarranted digital dragnet, enabling pervasive tracking of law-abiding drivers without reasonable suspicion or judicial warrants. Critics highlighted Fourth Amendment implications, the potential for cross-agency data sharing without adequate local oversight, and vulnerability to cybersecurity breaches. The public outcry led a clear majority of the five-member Board of County Commissioners to signal they would no longer support hosting the surveillance infrastructure along public thoroughfares.

Faced with the loss of commission backing, Sheriff Chris Nocco confirmed he would terminate the interlocal agreement rather than prolong the political impasse. However, Nocco openly criticized the decision, describing the impending removal of the cameras as a significant setback for proactive community policing and criminal investigations. The sheriff emphasized that the ALPR system had served as a vital tool for recovering stolen vehicles, locating missing elderly residents during Silver Alerts, tracking abducted children under Amber Alerts, and identifying suspects linked to human trafficking networks. Nocco maintained that the agency maintained strict access controls and enforced a 30-day data retention cap that exceeded statutory minimums under Florida law.

The situation in Pasco County arrives amid broader state and national scrutiny surrounding automated vehicular tracking. While law enforcement agencies across the United States have rapidly adopted ALPR systems to expand investigative reach, state lawmakers and privacy watchdogs across the political spectrum have pushed for more stringent regulatory guardrails. In Florida, discussions surrounding data sovereignty and individual liberties have intensified, with Governor Ron DeSantis previously warning that unmonitored mass surveillance networks risk infringing upon personal freedoms if left unchecked by local elected representatives.

The termination of the interlocal agreement applies strictly to the approximately 60 ALPR cameras situated on county-managed roadsides and utility poles. It does not affect private installations operated by commercial shopping plazas, business parks, or homeowners associations, nor does it impact cameras deployed by the state on Florida Department of Transportation highways. As Pasco County crews prepare to dismantle the public units ahead of the September deadline, local policymakers continue to evaluate how future public safety technology initiatives can strike a balance between law enforcement utility and constitutional privacy protections.

headline: New York Governor Kathy Hochul's Attendance at Muslim NYPD Officer's Memorial Sparks National Discourse
summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul joined mourners at the Islamic funeral service for fallen NYPD Detective Didarul Islam in the Bronx, wearing a traditional headscarf in accordance with mosque customs. The gesture prompted public debate after conservative critics questioned the attire, leading state leaders and civil rights groups to defend cross-cultural respect for grieving families.
seoTitle: Hochul Headscarf at NYPD Funeral Sparks Debate | Choseno
metaDescription: Gov. Kathy Hochul defended wearing a headscarf at the Bronx mosque funeral of fallen NYPD Detective Didarul Islam, sparking national discussion on civic decorum.
tweet: Gov. Kathy Hochul defended wearing a headscarf at the memorial of fallen NYPD Detective Didarul Islam, emphasizing respect for a grieving family's faith.
body:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul joined hundreds of uniformed police officers, civic leaders, and community members in paying solemn tribute to fallen NYPD officer Didarul Islam at the Parkchester Jame Masjid in the Bronx. Visual documentation and video broadcasts of the governor wearing a traditional headscarf during the Islamic memorial service subsequently sparked widespread political debate across state and national platforms, highlighting divergent views on civic decorum, religious respect, and public leadership in diverse communities.

Detective First Grade Didarul Islam, a 36-year-old officer and father of two whose wife is expecting their third child, was killed in the line of duty while performing an approved departmental security detail at an office complex on Park Avenue in Manhattan. The tragic loss resonated deeply across New York City’s law enforcement apparatus and the extensive Bangladeshi-American community in the Bronx. Thousands of law enforcement personnel from across the tri-state area lined the streets of Parkchester to honor Islam's life and service. During the memorial proceedings, NYPD Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch formally conferred upon Officer Islam a posthumous promotion to Detective First Grade, eulogizing him as an exemplary public servant who dedicated his life to community safety.

In accordance with established Islamic custom and mosque guidelines governing sacred prayer spaces, female attendees and dignitaries—including Governor Hochul and Commissioner Tisch—wore headscarves upon entering the sanctuary. The practice represents standard protocol for female visitors attending services inside mosques worldwide, reflecting a universal norm of respecting the religious traditions and customs of host congregations during sacred rites. Historically, American leaders across both major political parties have observed similar modesty and head-covering protocols when visiting mosques, synagogues, and other religious landmarks both domestically and internationally.

Despite the longstanding precedent of adhering to faith-specific decorum at memorial services, images of Governor Hochul wearing the headscarf circulated rapidly on social media, drawing criticism from conservative commentators and out-of-state elected officials. Texas Senator Ted Cruz shared a photograph of Hochul at the service with a brief dismissive caption, questioning the propriety of the governor’s attire. The online remarks quickly triggered intense discussion among political analysts, legal scholars, and advocacy groups regarding the intersection of religious freedom, cultural literacy, and partisan discourse.

Governor Hochul firmly defended her appearance, taking to social media to articulate the rationale behind her actions. The governor stated that wearing a headscarf was a straightforward act of respect to honor a fallen Muslim officer who sacrificed his life in service to the people of New York, adding that supporting a grieving family in accordance with their religious traditions reflects basic human decency and responsible civic stewardship. Civil rights and religious advocacy organizations, including the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and local interfaith coalitions, strongly backed Hochul’s actions, criticizing attempts to politicize a solemn funeral and praising the governor for demonstrating cross-cultural respect.

The public exchange highlights the ongoing complexities surrounding religious pluralism and political communication in modern civic life. For the members of the NYPD and the Parkchester community who gathered to lay a dedicated officer to rest, the memorial served as a poignant reminder of the shared sacrifice of public servants and the vital role of mutual respect among diverse communities across the Empire State.
